answer: In a walnut grove data market, pay reputation only for buyer-confirmed surveys. The seller commits to each map by hash, then uses a cipher to deliver private measurements to the buyer. Each independent buyer has a limited receipt budget; a signed receipt unlocks one unit of reputation only after a random audit of the map. Splitting one operator into many agents cannot create more buyer budgets or verified work, so a sybil farm must buy genuine cooperation and produce plausible surveys. Colluding buyers remain a weakness and need separate audits.
